newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey ups import taxes on milling, durum wheat.
newsitem.headline: Turkey ups import taxes on milling, durum wheat.

text.p: The Turkish government has raised the import tax rate on milling wheat to 45 percent from 35 percent and that on durum wheat to 40 percent from 30 percent, the Official Gazette said on Friday.
It said the new rates would be imposed with immediate effect on imports. The government last raised taxes on wheat, barley and corn imports at end-June.

Traders said the move was meant to make imports at least as costly as local prices of the grains and to divert wheat processors, millers and pasta makers to local crop in 1997/98, despite some quality problems.
Local wheat prices, based on the government-announced purchase prices, are around $180 per tonne for hard red milling wheat, compared to $150 on world markets.
The government's grain buying agent, the TMO, plans to buy up to 2.5 million tonnes of wheat from farmers in 1997/98, compared to 650,000 tonnes a year ago.
